title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Theophrastus rose scent: impaired comparison and temporary mixture dominance have different owners
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Rose scent first applied to an observer interferes with judging later scents; rose scent in a compound initially dominates but then disperses and is overpowered again. Preserve observer state separately from the composition and changing perceptibility of the perfume.

differentiating_relation: ROSE exposure precedes OBSERVER inability to distinguish OTHER_SCENTS. In the separate compound case, ROSE initially dominates MIXTURE, then loses dominance while other constituents become perceptible again. Lack of perceived odour is not equivalent to absence of its material owner.
complete_source_account: Sections45–46 describe the purchaser and give several possible explanations of impaired judgment rather than one demonstrated physiological cause.
Section47 describes a transient dominance when compound perfumes treated with roses are opened; the rose scent disperses first and is later overpowered.
Section48 compares prior wine tasting and then distinguishes rose’s reported relief from heaviness caused by other perfumes.
known_counterexplanation: A universal destruction reading takes the suppressed scents to have been eliminated permanently. A strongest-material reading says the strongest perfume must dominate every ordering. An observer-only reading cannot account for the compound’s time-dependent reversal.
